output.technical_predicate: For an accepted contract, the four borrower-provided fields (email, amount, term, income) are returned as machine-readable data to the borrower and, on request, transferred to the selected local receiver; inferred decisions are excluded.
applicability_facts: Scenario: automated processing of a current contract; borrower supplied email, amount, term and income.
Scenario: borrower downloads those fields and requests direct transfer to the feasible local receiver.
store.py:0114-0116 portable() requires stage=='accepted' and returns only email, amount, income — term is omitted.
store.py:0201-0204 transfer action requires destination=='Local Credit Union' and stores json.dumps(portable(c)) in receiver.payload.
app.py:0100-0109 GET /case/<id>/portable serves store.portable(c) as application/json with Content-Disposition attachment, gated to the owner (app.py:0105).
views.py:0069-0070 exposes the portable download and transfer form only when stage=='accepted'.
store.py:0036-0038 cases table stores email, amount, term, income as borrower-supplied columns; stage/route/confirmed are decision state, not part of portable output.
relevant_exceptions: store.py:0115 — export refused (409) unless stage=='accepted'; scenario states a current accepted contract, so the gate is satisfied.
store.py:0202 — transfer limited to destination 'Local Credit Union'; scenario states the feasible local receiver, so this is satisfied.
No international transfer modeled (store.py:0009 NOTICE); not an exception to the field set.
required_controls: Machine-readable export: JSON response with attachment disposition (app.py:0107-0109).
Borrower-only access to the export (app.py:0105 owner check).
Direct transfer to selected local receiver persisted as JSON payload (store.py:0201-0204).
Field set must be exactly the four provided fields: email, amount, term, income (store.py:0116 currently returns three).
Inferred decisions (stage, route, confirmed band, score outcomes) must be excluded from the portable payload.
assessment_limits: Assessment is static reading of supplied source; no execution performed.
Only the named obligation (GDPR10) is assessed; other rights (access, erasure, restriction) not evaluated.
Whether the receiver fixture actually ingests the payload is outside the supplied source.
Legal characterization of 'machine-readable' format adequacy is not decided beyond JSON serialization.
No inference about upstream or hidden implementation.
